prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a polished SIX-PANEL CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET for an original children's book talking bath duck. Landscape image divided into tidy 3 columns by 2 rows, generous clear equal-sized panels with soft cream background and subtle warm shadow, no lettering or captions. Reference images show the EXACT same small CARVED WOODEN duck: rounded honeywood body, rounded head on short neck, orange wooden broad beak, tiny shiny dark eyes, carved wing panels with incised feather lines, small raised pointed tail. Preserve its wood grain, knots, hand-carved soft edges, exact toy shape and proportions; absolutely no feathers, rubber or plastic skin, human body, legs, hands or extra arms. It has become expressive through a magically flexible orange beak, tiny eyelids, attentive gaze and slight head/body tilts, while remaining clearly this same wooden bath toy. Warm dimensional animated-feature storybook rendering identical to references, tactile wood, gentle attractive light. Render six views/expressions of same toy at consistent scale: top-left calm attentive three-quarter normal closed beak; top-middle delighted gently smiling open beak looking upward to a child; top-right speaking/quacking with small open orange beak, gaze directly toward viewer; bottom-left surprised by a splash, little widened eyes and open beak, tiny water droplets; bottom-middle spirited determined helpful expression, head leaning forward while floating on small ripple; bottom-right cozy amused duck tucked in a small cream towel, HEAD and whole orange beak visible, toy body partly wrapped but no hands holding towel. No speech balloons, no symbols, no badges, no text, no other characters. Keep exact wooden duck identity across all six, not six different species. Expressive face should read at children's book size without turning into human face.
